newsitem.title: USA: Supervalu FY97 retail earnings improve.
newsitem.headline: Supervalu FY97 retail earnings improve.

text.p: Supervalu Inc said Thursday fiscal 1997 earnings rose due to improvements in its retail operations, while its wholesale business was hurt by increased costs for changes in its distribution system.
Retail food operating earnings rose 64 percent to $93.7 million for the year, and increased 43 percent to $31.7 million for the fourth quarter ended February 22, 1997.
Retail food sales increased seven percent to $4.7 billion for the year and rose eight percent to $1.2 billion for the quarter. At fiscal year-end, the company operated 322 corporate stores.

Supervalu said its food distribution operating earnings were $310.5 million for the fiscal 1997, down from $334.7 million a year ago. For the fourth quarter, food distribution earnings dropped to $72.8 million from $75.0 million.
Earlier, Supervalu reported earnings for the full year of $2.60 a share, up from $2.44. For the fourth quarter, it earned $0.79 a share, up from $0.72.

Supervalu said its capital budget for fiscal 1998 was set at $400 million, down from $436 million in fiscal 1997. The 1998 budget includes $365 million of cash spending plus $35 million of capital leases.

About $200 million of the fiscal 1998 capital budget is slated for the food distribution segment, the company said. Projects include a new perishable warehouse, the construction of several small distribution centers for its Save-A-Lot stores, the construction of a Midwest regional distribution center, development and implementation of information technology, and normal replacement spending.
